The '@11' prefix filter also catches the block's instruction column ('@11, there are 20 statements, please choose to best describe the last week'), which the export left as the header of the block's FIRST item; the script prepends the unprefixed column instead, so the shipped order is source columns 29,28,30,31,...,47 and CESD_1/CESD_2 are the canonical CES-D items 2 and 1 respectively. Corroborated independently -- recoding 1-4 to 0-3 and reversing {CESD_4,CESD_8,CESD_12,CESD_16} (the canonical positive-affect quadruple at canonical positions 4,8,12,16) reproduces the workbook's own precomputed CESD total for 494/494 respondents, against 41/494 with no reversal and at best 142/494 for any reverse set with one item swapped. So the block is a complete, canonically ordered 20-item CES-D and the unlabelled column can only be item 1. (3) TRANSCRIPTION DEVIATIONS, all deliberate: the '@11. ' / '@11, ' export prefix was stripped from every header, and pandas' duplicate-column suffix '.1' was stripped from CESD_18 ('I feel sad.1'). Nothing else was altered -- the source's own rough English, missing terminal punctuation and duplicate rendering of items 6 and 18 as 'I feel sad' are shipped as written. (4) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: administered to 494 Chinese undergraduates across 25 provinces. The article has exactly ONE supplementary file (S1 Data, sha256 8a2cc778ce20aafd8d9dd1a463c54f7e211b83e48b59a9c5cec3d997b62f1f21) and it contains ZERO CJK characters in any header or any cell, so no administered Chinese wording exists in scope.
